summary.intent: Research how the TDAD paper and Curtis's spec-driven UI article apply to the agent-plugins repo, then rename the plugin family with a memorable persona-based naming scheme (adding a frontend/design plugin for Lumen), and simplify agent prompts based on the findings (drop mandatory test-first ordering, bulletize prose, reduce over-prescription).
summary.outcome: Ran two multi-agent research workflows producing prioritized integration proposals. The family was renamed to the 'Wisp' umbrella with 10 persona plugins including a new `muse`, and that rename merged as PR #1. Test-first ordering was removed from smith/navigator (ADR-008), 21 agent judgment sections were bulletized, and implementer shape latitude plus compilation-boundary task sizing were added (ADR-009). All of it is on PR #2, which is green and targets main.

repo: Plugin family is now Wisp: loom/weaver, lantern/vanguard, oracle/scribe, navigator, smith, ranger, sentinel, courier, mason, muse. Directory names are the shipped personas, e.g. plugins/smith, plugins/navigator, plugins/scribe.

Every plugin version change must be synced across plugin.json, README masthead, CHANGELOG, both marketplace files, and the root marketplace/README badge/CHANGELOG. scripts/check-versions.sh and shared/scripts/validate-wiring.sh enforce this.

Repo precedent is to record significant behavior changes as ADRs in docs/adr/ (008 drop-test-first-ordering, 009 implementer-shape-latitude) and not to rewrite historical ADRs such as ADR-003; cross-reference them instead.
shared/constitution.md reserves EARS notation for <constitution>/<output> sections. A grep confirmed it hasn't leaked into backstory/goal/judgment across the 41 agent files.
The constitution block is byte-identical across agents and prompt-cached, so per-agent unique content (backstory/goal/judgment) is where context cost actually accrues.
shared/agent-best-practices.md already had a batching rule contradicting the planner's '15 minute task' cap; the cap was replaced with compilation-boundary sizing.

Research-workflow critique rejected speculative new schemas/plugins (component-spec@1, swatch) because no producer or consumer existed. Surviving proposals were extensions of proof/canon (a11y hazard taxonomy, drafter component-criterion guidance, token-drift smells).

code.finding: Planner previously mandated exact implementation code per task and a 15-minute task cap; both were reframed (code as baseline, compilation-boundary sizing). Line numbers weren't given in the transcript.
Has an 'over-specified' check dimension that only catches cosmetic rigidity (private variable naming), not structural over-prescription like mandatory exact code.
Judgment section was rewritten for no-test-first flow but not bulletized until a later pass. It was wrongly described as already bulletized when briefing subagents.

workflow: Verify primary sources directly. Fetching Böckeler's article corrected an earlier second-hand paraphrase: TDD cost 2.96-8.5x more tokens with no quality gain, and the effect traces to test-first ordering rather than the presence of tests.

Parallel subagent passes with a precise worked example and an explicit 'leave alone if no 2+ enumeration' rule produced consistent mechanical refactors. Spot-checking the agents' self-flagged judgment calls was worthwhile.
Checking PR state directly rather than assuming (PR #1 had merged externally) caught a stale base branch, which was fixed by retargeting PR #2 to main.
Unexpected untracked files (.codex/hooks.json) were inspected and excluded before the commit, then committed separately once the user asked.
Adversarial critique passes in the research workflows were effective at rejecting speculative infrastructure.

friction: Naming took many rounds (Muse, Hachi/Apis/Agora, Genii, Familiar, finally Wisp) because early suggestions were too dictionary-derived or constrained to bee imagery.
A hard constraint emerged mid-conversation that the user wanted to avoid one name family and famous-engineer names, forcing re-proposals.
Earlier edits left a stray covers_criteria bullet and a wrong relative path in navigator SKILL.md; both were caught and fixed later.
The assistant misreported implementer.md as already bulletized, which only surfaced on later review.
Workflow output was truncated in notifications, so the full report had to be read from the output file.
The initial grep for TDD-ordering mentions missed alternate phrasings, which needed additional sweeps.
open_items: Backend research proposals remain unbuilt: check-schema-refs.sh, check-schema-immutability.sh, check-plugin-agents.sh, a verdict@3 regressions[] evidence trail, canon/scribe drift-checker severity tiering, an axiom/sentinel downstream-consumer check, and reviewer search-backed sibling-gap enumeration.

FE work for Lumen is not yet implemented: the proof/ranger a11y hazard taxonomy (typescript-hazards-a11y.md), token-drift smells, and muse/drafter component-criterion guidance were only partially or not at all built.
The basis/mason calibrator is gated on a manual auditor.md simplification pilot with fixtures, to be done before any automation.
Whether backstory narratives should be bulletized is an open question, to be settled by an outcome-measured pilot rather than by feel.
The pilot for dropping test-first ordering needs measurement against real Smith tasks (cost and quality).
A GIVEN/WHEN/SHALL (EARS-plus-context) acceptance-criteria phrasing for scribe/muse drafters and navigator's planner was proposed, with the user's go-ahead unclear.
Add a Define/Design/Build/Verify/Ship category-band table to the README, and make sure every name is paired with a role tag (especially muse, to avoid the mockup-generation reading).
PR #2 (3+ commits) is awaiting review and merge.
